key_insight: Multilingual multimodal machine learning can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech.
clinical_relevance: This could help speed up and standardize differential diagnosis for bilingual patients when language-specific expert assessment is limited.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients were recorded describing a picture in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Four feature sets were extracted from speech: timing, word-level, linguistic, and image-text congruence features.
Multiple classifiers and an ensemble model were tested to separate nfvPPA from lvPPA.
evidence_signal: In this 34-patient study, the best model reached 93% macro-F1 in the non-dominant language and 92% in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: Small sample size and single-prompt, bilingual-specific testing may limit generalizability and require external validation before routine use.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
